# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 13 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 13
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. But let us further inquire whether this people or the former people is the heir, and whether the covenant belongs to us or to them.
2. Hear then what the scripture says concerning the people: "And Isaac prayed for Rebecca his wife, because she was barren; and she conceived. Then Rebecca went out to inquire of the Lord, and the Lord said to her: 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples in your belly; and one people shall have dominion over the other, and the greater shall serve the lesser.'"
3. You ought to understand who is signified by Isaac, and who by Rebecca, and of whom he has shown that this people is greater than that people.
4. And in another prophecy, Jacob speaks more clearly to Joseph his son, saying: "Behold, the Lord has not deprived me of seeing your face; bring your sons to me that I may bless them."
5. And Joseph brought Ephraim and Manasseh, desiring that Manasseh, being the firstborn, should be blessed; and so Joseph brought him to the right hand of his father Jacob. And Jacob saw in the Spirit a type of the future people — and what did he do? He crossed his hands and placed his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, the second-born and the younger, and blessed him. And Joseph said to Jacob: "Move your right hand to the head of Manasseh, for he is my firstborn son." And Jacob said to Joseph: "I know, my child, I know; but the greater shall serve the lesser — and he also shall be blessed."
6. See for whom he ordained that this people should be first and the heir of the covenant.
7. If, therefore, this was also remembered and established from the beginning through Abraham, then we are the people of the inheritance, the truly first people.

---

## Council Notes

- v.2: Genesis 25:21-23 (LXX). The oracle to Rebecca is read typologically: the older/greater nation (Israel) serves the younger/lesser nation (the church). This supersessionist reading reverses the historical priority of Israel.
- vv.4-5: Genesis 48:9-19 — Jacob's crossed-hands blessing. Jacob's deliberate crossing of his arms to bless Ephraim over Manasseh is read as a prophetic type of the cross (the crossed arms = the cross) and of the reversal of the elder-serves-younger pattern.
- v.7: "We are the people of the inheritance, the truly first people" — *hēmeis... protos laos* — this is the culmination of Barnabas's argument: Christians are not a new people but the *original* people, the people God always intended to bless, hidden under the surface of Israel's history.
- Hermeneutical note: The older-serves-younger motif (Cain/Abel, Ishmael/Isaac, Esau/Jacob, Manasseh/Ephraim) is read as a consistent pattern pointing toward the supersession of the first covenant by the second. Paul makes a similar but more restrained argument in Romans 9:10-13.
